_note: Original practice items written for the Classic EDU Suite CBT bank. Not reproduced from any past paper. Syllabus-aligned to JAMB Principles of Accounts / Financial Accounting.

questions.question: Accounting may best be described as the process of
options: counting the physical assets of a business
identifying, recording, classifying and reporting financial information
questions.explanation: Book-keeping records transactions; accounting also classifies, summarises and interprets them.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The accounting equation is correctly stated as
questions.explanation: Everything the business owns is financed either by the owner or by outsiders.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: If the assets of a business are ₦500,000 and its liabilities are ₦200,000, the capital is
questions.explanation: Capital = assets − liabilities = 500,000 − 200,000 = ₦300,000.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The principle of double entry means that every transaction
options: is recorded twice in the same account
must be approved by two persons
is recorded only in the cash book
affects two accounts, one debited and the other credited
questions.explanation: For every debit entry there must be a corresponding credit entry of equal amount.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A book in which transactions are recorded for the first time is called a
questions.explanation: Journals and day books are books of original or prime entry.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Credit purchases of goods are recorded in the
questions.explanation: Only credit purchases of goods for resale enter the purchases day book.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The cash book is best described as
options: both a book of original entry and a ledger
a book of original entry only
questions.explanation: It records transactions first and also serves as the cash and bank ledger accounts.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A two-column cash book is used to record
questions.explanation: One column is for cash in hand and the other for the bank balance.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Discount allowed is treated in the final accounts as
questions.explanation: It is a cost of obtaining prompt payment and is debited to profit and loss.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The petty cash book is normally operated on the
questions.explanation: The petty cashier is reimbursed exactly what was spent, restoring the fixed float.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A debit entry in an account records
questions.explanation: Debit increases assets and expenses; credit increases liabilities, capital and income.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A credit entry in an account records
options: an increase in a liability or capital
questions.explanation: Liabilities, capital and revenue all increase on the credit side.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The trial balance is prepared mainly to
options: determine the profit for the period
show the financial position of the business
check the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger
questions.explanation: If total debits equal total credits, the postings are arithmetically in agreement.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Which of the following errors will NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?
options: Omitting one side of a transaction
Entering different amounts on each side
Error of complete omission of a transaction
questions.explanation: If the transaction is left out entirely, both sides remain equal.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Posting ₦500 to the account of the wrong customer, although in the correct class of account, is an error of
questions.explanation: An error of commission puts a correct amount in the wrong account of the right type.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Treating the purchase of a motor vehicle as a motor running expense is an error of
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure has been wrongly recorded as revenue expenditure.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A suspense account is opened in order to
options: hold the profit of the business
record temporarily the difference in the trial balance
questions.explanation: It balances the trial balance until the errors are traced and corrected.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The purchase of a delivery van for use in the business is
questions.explanation: It acquires a fixed asset whose benefit lasts beyond the current period.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Payment for fuel used by the company's delivery van is
questions.explanation: It is consumed within the period and is charged against the period's profit.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Gross profit is calculated as
options: net sales minus cost of goods sold
questions.explanation: Gross profit is found in the trading account before other expenses are deducted.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Opening stock is ₦20,000, purchases ₦150,000 and closing stock ₦30,000. Calculate the cost of goods sold.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Sales are ₦200,000 and the cost of goods sold is ₦140,000. Calculate the gross profit.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Gross profit is ₦60,000 and total expenses are ₦25,000. Calculate the net profit.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The trading account is prepared in order to determine the
questions.explanation: The profit and loss account then determines net profit.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Carriage inwards is charged to the
questions.explanation: It is part of the cost of bringing in goods purchased and so increases cost of sales.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Carriage outwards is charged to the
questions.explanation: It is a selling and distribution expense, not part of the cost of goods purchased.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A balance sheet shows the
options: cash received and paid during a period
gross and net profit for the year
income and expenditure for a period
assets, liabilities and capital at a particular date
questions.explanation: It is a statement of position at one moment in time, not for a period.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Fixed assets are assets
options: bought specifically for resale at a profit
acquired for long-term use in the business
that can be converted to cash within days
questions.explanation: Land, buildings, plant and vehicles are held to be used, not to be resold.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Working capital is calculated as
questions.explanation: It measures the funds available for day-to-day operations.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Current assets are ₦80,000 and current liabilities are ₦30,000. Calculate the working capital.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Depreciation is best described as the
options: reduction in the value of a fixed asset through use and the passage of time
fall in the market price of stock
loss made on the sale of goods
cash set aside to replace an asset
questions.explanation: It allocates the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Under the straight-line method, the depreciation charge each year is
options: based on the market value each year
questions.explanation: The cost less scrap value is spread evenly over the asset's useful life.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A machine costing ₦100,000 has an estimated scrap value of ₦10,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Calculate the annual depreciation using the straight-line method.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: An asset costing ₦200,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum using the reducing balance method. Calculate the depreciation charge for the second year.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Bad debts written off during the year are
options: added to debtors in the balance sheet
charged to the profit and loss account
questions.explanation: The irrecoverable amount is an expense of the period in which it is written off.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: In the balance sheet, the provision for doubtful debts is
questions.explanation: Debtors are shown at the amount expected to be collected.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Rent paid in advance at the end of the accounting year is treated as
options: an expense of the current year
questions.explanation: A prepayment is a benefit still to be received, so it is an asset.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Wages owing to employees at the end of the accounting year are treated as
questions.explanation: An accrued expense is an amount owed and therefore a liability.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared to reconcile the
options: cash book balance with the bank statement balance
trial balance with the balance sheet
petty cash float with the main cash book
sales ledger with the purchases ledger
questions.explanation: It explains differences caused by timing and by items known to only one party.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: An unpresented cheque is one that has been
options: drawn and recorded but not yet paid by the bank
questions.explanation: The cash book already shows the payment, but the bank statement does not yet.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The sales ledger control account is used to show the total
options: stock held at the year end
questions.explanation: It summarises the individual accounts in the sales (debtors) ledger.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: In the absence of any agreement to the contrary, partnership profits are shared
options: according to the age of the partners
questions.explanation: Where there is no agreement, the law presumes profits and losses are shared equally.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Interest on partners' capital is
questions.explanation: It is an appropriation of profit, not an expense of running the business.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The partnership appropriation account shows
options: how the net profit is divided among the partners
the gross profit of the firm
the assets and liabilities of the firm
the cash movements of the firm
questions.explanation: Salaries, interest on capital and profit shares are dealt with there.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The authorised capital of a company is the
options: maximum amount of share capital it may issue
questions.explanation: It is stated in the memorandum and sets a ceiling on the shares that may be issued.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Preference shareholders normally
options: receive a fixed rate of dividend
control the voting at general meetings
receive a share of profit that varies each year
questions.explanation: They rank ahead of ordinary shareholders for dividend and capital repayment.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Current assets are ₦80,000 and current liabilities are ₦40,000. Calculate the current ratio.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: The accounting concept which assumes that a business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future is the
questions.explanation: It justifies showing assets at cost less depreciation rather than at break-up value.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: Recognising revenue when it is earned rather than when cash is received illustrates the
questions.explanation: Income and expenses are matched to the period to which they relate.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts

questions.question: A receipts and payments account is normally prepared by
questions.explanation: Clubs and societies summarise their cash transactions in this way.
questions.subject: Principles of Accounts
